title: streaming-sse-chunking-backpressure-debug-notes-taylor
content:
TL;DR: Intermittent client disconnects and apparent stalled streams when the server emits SSE events at high rate. Symptoms look like chunked-transfer buffering at the proxy (Envoy/nginx) + client backpressure (read loop not keeping up). Repro steps below + commands I tried and notes on hypotheses and mitigations.

Symptom summary:
- Client sees stream stall ~5-20s into a high-throughput session; connection sometimes closed by server.
- Server logs: no obvious errors, but GC spikes align with stalls.
- Proxy (Envoy) metrics show increased upstream_cx_active and high buffer_bytes for the route during incidents.
- Curl with --no-buffer often shows data fine; browsers sometimes buffer until larger chunks arrive.

Quick repro (simple):
1) Start simple SSE emitter (node) that writes an event every 10ms:
   node simple-sse.js  # script below

simple-sse.js (local repro script):
const http = require('http');
http.createServer((req, res) => {
  res.writeHead(200, {
    'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream',
    'Cache-Control': 'no-cache',
    'Connection': 'keep-alive',
    'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no' // try to disable nginx buffering
  });
  let i = 0;
  const t = setInterval(() => {
    res.write(`id: ${i}
event: tick
data: { "n": ${i} }

`);
    i++;
    if (i > 10000) { clearInterval(t); res.end(); }
  }, 10);
}).listen(8080);

2) Repro client attempts:
- curl -N http://localhost:8080 | sed -u 's/^/CURL: /'  # -N disables buffering
- httpie: http --stream GET http://localhost:8080
- node client-read.js (see below)
- Python requests with stream=True

node client-read.js:
const http = require('http');
http.get('http://localhost:8080', res => {
  res.on('data', chunk => {
    process.stdout.write(`got ${chunk.length} bytes
`);
  });
});

Observed behavior locally:
- On bare localhost everything is fine (curl, node client).
- When put behind local nginx reverse proxy with default settings, client sees bursts: nothing for ~1s then many events at once. Looks like proxy buffering.
- Adding header X-Accel-Buffering: no helps for nginx (confirmed) but only when proxy config honors it (we have multiple proxies; not all honor).

Commands I ran (troubleshooting):
- curl -v -N http://host/route  # to see headers and chunking
- ngrep -W byline port 80 'HTTP'  # watch raw bytes across proxy
- tcpdump -i lo -s 0 -A port 8080  # confirm chunk boundaries from app
- strace -tt -e write -p <pid>  # timing of write syscalls in runtime
- sudo ss -tin sport = :8080  # socket buffers and state
- wrk -t2 -c50 -d20s --latency 'http://host/route'  # load test for reproduction

Error snippets seen in clients/logs:
- Browser console: "EventSource connection failed" / 404 sometimes when our routing returns 502 briefly.
- Node client: ECONNRESET when upstream closes connection after buffer fills.
- nginx error log (rare): "upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream"
- Occasionally see "ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING" in some http libraries (indicates abrupt close).

Observations and measurements:
- Server write cadence: every 10ms, payload ~200B -> ~20KB/s per stream. At 200 concurrent streams this becomes 4MB/s.
- GC pauses (Node Hotspot) ~20-50ms observed when heap grows; if pause overlaps with burst it can delay writes and allow proxy buffers to coalesce chunks.
- Envoy has per-connection buffers; default behavior can buffer until certain thresholds.
- When we set response.flushHeaders() and res.flush() (in Node via compression middleware or using express with res.flush) we see reduced coalescing.

Hypotheses:
1) Proxy buffering is the dominant factor: Envoy/nginx is coalescing small writes into larger buffered writes to clients. When client side backpressure causes the proxy to hold data, the upstream may eventually be closed or time out.
2) Server-side GC / event loop stalls make timely writes inconsistent, which interacts badly with proxy buffering thresholds.
3) Client read loop is not optimized (small highWaterMark or blocking processing) causing backpressure signaled to the proxy and upstream.
4) Transfer-Encoding vs SSE framing: missing final "
\nWhat I tried (and results):
- Set X-Accel-Buffering: no on responses -> nginx honored and buffering reduced; behavior better for that proxy.
- For Envoy routes: tried setting "use_remote_address" and tuned per-route buffer limits; confirmed envoy metric "upstream_flow_control_paused_reading" increments.
- Increased Node writable stream highWaterMark to allow app-level buffering without blocking write calls: helped reduce ECONNRESET frequency but increased memory.
- Reduced payload size and frequency (every 50ms) -> fewer stalls. Not ideal.
- Enabled HTTP/2 for the route -> different behavior: some clients (EventSource) don't support HTTP/2 SSE well; not compatible.
- Added backpressure-aware client that parses SSE incrementally and does minimal processing in data handler -> removes client-side stall.

Repro commands that reliably show the problem (behind proxy):
1) Start server (simple-sse.js on :8080)
2) Configure local nginx reverse proxy with default config proxying /sse -> localhost:8080\3) Run: wrk -t2 -c100 -d20s --latency 'http://localhost/sse'  # creates many concurrent SSE subscribers
4) Watch nginx access/error log and app stdout for intermittent ECONNRESET / aborted writes
5) tcpdump -i lo -s 0 -A port 8080 will show delayed chunks (server wrote small chunks but network packer shows bigger aggregated chunks).

Immediate mitigations to try in prod (low risk, incremental):
- Add X-Accel-Buffering: no and X-Request-Buffered: false equivalents on upstream responses where possible (Envoy needs per-route config).
- Tune Envoy buffer limits for the SSE route (increase per-connection buffer or disable buffering for that route).
- Add a middleware to ensure we flush after every event (res.flushHeaders() + write + drain handling).
- Implement a simple rate limiter per connection so momentary GC spikes don't create large bursts.
- Instrument GC/heap and add alerts for long GC pause times aligned with stream incidents.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Try reproducing with Redwood serving-runtime stack: test route through staging Envoy + autoscaler to verify buffering is same as prod.
- [ ] Open a short PR adding X-Accel-Buffering: no for SSE endpoints and a note in the runtime docs. (See GH-PR-4523)
- [ ] Work with infra to identify which proxies (ELB -> ALB -> Envoy) exist on the path; add per-hop configs.
- [ ] Add a small e2e test that subscribes to SSE and measures per-event latency under load (wrk-driven).
- [ ] If proxies cannot be configured, implement server-side periodic keepalives with larger chunks to keep proxy flush behavior consistent.

Notes / random findings:
- curl -N is useful for quick tests but not identical to browsers' EventSource behavior.
- Some libs only treat CRLF CRLF as event terminator; ensure exactly one blank line between events.
- When using gzip compression on the route, proxies will buffer until compression window fills -> avoid compressing SSE responses.

If anyone wants to pair on repro in staging, ping me (Taylor).

Attachments / snippets I used: wrk command lines, node repro script above, simple nginx conf snippet with proxy_buffering off (can paste if useful).

End of notes.
